Council Minutes  1  02/23/2026
   The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4): Four potential cases

  Two of the four cases from Closed Session Item E were discussed,
  with no reportable action taken for one of the cases at this time. For
  the second case, the City Council voted to enter as an amicus curiae
  in support of the plaintiffs in the matter of Barbara, et. al. v. Trump
  against the following parties: President Donald J. Trump, U.S.
  Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Department of State, U.S.
  Department of Agriculture, U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid
  Services; U.S. Administrator for the Centers for Medicare and
  Medicaid Semces; U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security, U.S.
  Secretary of State, and U.S. Secretary of Agriculture. The litigation
  challenges Presidential Executive Order 14160, which denies
  birthright United States citizenship to children born in the US after
  February 20, 2025 to parents who are undocumented or temporarily
  present in the US.

  It was moved by Councilmember Cole, seconded by Councilmember
  Jones, to authorize the City to join as amicus curiae. (Motion
  unanimously approved) (Absent: Councilmember Lyon)

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding significant exposure to potential litigation pursuant
  to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): One potential case

  The above closed session item was discussed, with no reportable

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for the City to terminate all
  contracts with Flock cameras. Eugene Harris, Police Chief, stated
  that the City has not shared any information with Flock.

Council Minutes  3  02/23/2026
   Councilmember Hampton expressed concerns regarding reports of
  Flock camera data being shared with Federal agents, and asked that
  City staff review and investigate those reports, and return with
  information on whether data sharing has occurred.

  Councilmember Cole and Mayor Gordo distributed and reviewed a
  draft resolution entitled, "Proposed Pasadena City Council Actions
  to Mitigate the Impacts of Federal Civil Immigration Enforcement
  Overreach on City Resources, Property, and Community Safety",
  which includes 13 separate directions to the City staff on actions to
  mitigate immigration enforcement in the City.

  Vice Mayor Rivas expressed support for the draft resolution, and also
  advocated for the City to have a broader and more transparent
  discussion on how it has confirmed that the City's Flock camera data
  has not been accessed by the federal government for immigration
  enforcement purposes. She also noted that Pasadena Police
  Department may become aware of immigration enforcement
  activities after residents report such incidents, and suggested that
  City staff present monthly reports to the Public Safety Committee
  depicting the scale and magnitude of the federal activity in the City.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding the status of
  the City allocating $100,000 to support communities impacted by the
  federal immigration activities, City Manager Marquez reported that
  the initial effort to distribute funds was delayed due to the inability of
  the selected nonprofit to undertake the disbursement effort, and that
  the City is now working with the California Community Foundation to
  raise additional funds and disperse funds to other nonprofits in aid of
  those that need emergency assistance. hie also expressed support
  for monthly reporting of federal immigration activity in the City to the
  Public Safety Committee.

  Councilmember Madison advocated for the City to partner with local
  organizations or non-profits to provide training to community
  members on how to safely and lawfully observe immigration
  activities, and for Pasadena Police Officers to ensure legal
  boundaries are not crossed when responding to crimes potentially
  committed by federal immigration officers.

  Councilmember Lyon expressed support for the proposed resolution,
  as well as the suggested training for lawful observers and for
  Pasadena Police Officers to protect themselves from federal
  lawlessness. He advocated for the City to take expedited actions
  given the quick nature of the evolving crisis.

  Councilmember Masuda expressed support for the proposed
  resolution and emphasized the importance of respect and
  transparency between the City and residents to preserve public
  safety.

Council Minutes  4  02/23/2026
   Mayor Gordo noted two changes to the proposed resolution,
  amending verbiage in Item 4 to state "...to evaluate a ban on any
  use of City property by civil law enforcement immigration
r
  enforcement entities..." and in Item 11 "to develop suggested
  appropriate language for signage.. ."

  Councilmember Hampton expressed support for the resolution and
  asked that the City suspend existing contracts with Flock until City
  staff returns to the City Council with information on the cameras and
  data sharing. City Attorney Bagneris reported that since the Flock
  camera contract is not agendized, the City Council may only give
  direction for City staff to return with information.

  MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Cole,
  seconded by Councilmember Hampton, to approve the proposed
  draft resolution submitted by Mayor Gordo and Councilmember Cole
  to mitigate the impacts of federal civil immigration enforcement on
  City resources, property, and community safety (with direction to City
  staff to review and provide proposed recommendations on how to
  effectuate actions 1 through 13), approving amended language to
  action items 4 and 11, direct the Pasadena Police Department to
  report back on the Flock camera contracts at the next Public Safety
  Committee meeting, direct the Pasadena Police Department to
  provide monthly reporting to the Public Safety Committee on federal
  immigration enforcement occurring in the City, direct the City
  Manager to provide an update on the status of the $100,000
  previously allocated by the City Council to fund support to community
  members impacted by immigration enforcement, and direct City staff
  to identify training opportunities for Pasadena Police Officers,
  community members, and lawful observers on best practices to
  observe federal immigration activities to ensure their public safety
  and protection. (Motion unanimously approved) (Absent: None)
